A notification deep link requires a permission check as a const, and a delivery failure records that it did not roll back the domain result as a const -- both expressed in the contract rather than in prose. AMENDED 2026-10-06 (C0 head review B-6 and §7): the second half is WITHDRAWN. The `domain_result_rolled_back: const false` it describes was removed as a category error -- a const asserting what another subsystem did makes a truthful report of a real rollback schema-invalid -- and Decision Register 4.2 places the prohibition on MOD-100 (A5's module). What the contract expresses instead: `deep_link.requires_permission` is const true AND required, and a failed delivery must carry a failure_class while a delivered one must not. The non-rollback obligation is declared in CTR-NTF-001's untestable_by_schema.

PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06, verified against the tree; the three claims this entry made are answered separately and only two of them are closed. It read: 'This package depends on five unmerged packages and inherits every open blocker recorded on them, including that the test-integrity guard is a tripwire with no self-anchor and that npm run check can be neutered by its own script.' (a) UNMERGED IS FALSE. All five branches -- WP-0A-A0-002, WP-0A-CON-002, WP-0A-CON-003, WP-0A-CON-004 and WP-0A-CON-005 -- reached main, in pull requests #3 through #7 and later re-merges. The inheritance itself STANDS: all five still read status in_review, so every open blocker recorded on them is still open and still inherited by this package. (b) NEUTERED BY ITS OWN SCRIPT IS ANSWERED ON THE CI PATH ONLY. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `node scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs` as its own step, 'Verify test-integrity guard', before it runs `npm run check`, per RFC-2026-007 (Approved 2026-09-02). A guard the workflow invokes cannot be short-circuited by the scripts.check string. It is not answered for a local `npm run check`, where the chain still invokes its own guard and a trailing `&` or a chain of `||` still exits 0 having run nothing. (c) NO SELF-ANCHOR IS HALF ANSWERED, AND THE REMAINING HALF STAYS. An outside anchor now exists: branch protection on main has been real since 2026-09-02 -- strict required status check `bootstrap`, enforce_admins true, no force push, no branch deletion -- and it was tested rather than merely configured, a direct push by an admin being rejected with GH006 (evidence/g0-tracker-th.md). What has not changed is that the guard is a TRIPWIRE and not a control: a commit that edits a protected file and updates its digest in the same commit passes, the guard says so in its own exit-86 message, and the integrity manifest is the one unanchored artifact -- nothing inside this repository can verify it. No required pull-request review is configured either, because the Product Owner opens the pull requests and GitHub forbids approving your own, so the human half of the anchor is the Product Owner reading a diff rather than a control. Note for a reader who checks: OVERNIGHT-SUMMARY.md item 3 still describes protected CI as unavailable pending a paid plan. That file contradicts evidence/g0-tracker-th.md and the guard's own message, and it belongs to no package this run may amend. Text as recorded: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06 BY MEASUREMENT, not by memory. This entry read: 'The 30% mutation-coverage floor is a floor, not a target. The catalog sits at 42.4% and the weakest contract at 32.4%.' Every number in it is stale. The floor in test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs is now COVERAGE_FLOOR = 0.70, and its own comment records that when the metric was corrected to count assertion keywords only, the catalog figure the old metric reported as 42.4% was really 19.3% -- the old one counted bare property names as constraint sites. RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD: catalog 654 of 721 constraint sites killed by a declared fixture = 90.7%; weakest contract ctr-ntf-001 at 30 of 39 = 76.9%. Method, so it can be repeated: copy test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs and json-schema-subset.mjs to a scratch directory, change COVERAGE_FLOOR to 1.01 so that every contract is reported rather than only the failing ones, and run `node --test --test-name-pattern="mutation-coverage floor" <copy>` from the repository root; the per-contract killed/total pairs are in the assertion message and the catalog figure is their sum. Nothing in the repository was edited to measure this. WHAT THE ENTRY WAS FOR STILL STANDS: a floor is not a target. 67 constraint sites across the catalog are killed by no fixture at all, and each one is a rule that nothing exercises. A 70% floor against a measured 90.7% leaves twenty points in which coverage can regress with nothing failing; what actually holds the line is the per-contract UNKILLED_CEILING and SITE_FLOOR tables, which are exact and must be edited deliberately. Raising the floor is still cheap and should still be done as coverage rises. One consequence for a reader of this list: the '82% coverage' figure quoted in the next-but-one entry predates this measurement and was left untouched because it was not re-measured.

Roughly 71% of the 441 generated counterexamples are MECHANICAL -- they violate a rule with a sentinel value (`zz not matching pattern`) rather than with a value a producer could plausibly emit. Independent testing measured it and the judgement is accepted: the 66 enum, pattern and format fixtures are the weakest, because those keywords are exactly where a contract encodes a specific hazard and a sentinel erases it. They are load-bearing -- each one is a real witness that kills exactly one site -- but they are not documentation, and 82% coverage should not be read as 82% of the catalog's hazards being illustrated.
